inspiration.observed_pattern: A movie-database search applies the case-insensitive ILIKE predicate to movie names, people names, cast roles, and category names while retaining deterministic ordering.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a media-catalog report. MariaDB 10.11.7 expresses the same case-insensitive pattern with LOWER(column) LIKE LOWER(pattern), and the report returns matching entries plus per-kind counts. The schema, labels, values, and report shape are new.

fixture_notes: The search term matches mixed-case title text in film and book entries, leaves a nonmatching entry and a NULL title out, and counts matches by entry kind.
determinism_notes: Entry IDs, fixed titles, kinds, search pattern, grouping, and ordering are fixed. No clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE media_catalog (entry_id INT PRIMARY KEY, entry_title VARCHAR(96) NULL, entry_kind VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
INSERT INTO media_catalog VALUES (801, 'Hitchcock at Dusk', 'film'), (802, 'The HITCHHIKER Index', 'book'), (803, 'The Matrix', 'film'), (804, NULL, 'archive'), (805, 'HITCH Notes', 'archive')

steps.sql: SELECT entry_id, entry_title, entry_kind FROM media_catalog WHERE LOWER(entry_title) LIKE LOWER('%hitch%') ORDER BY entry_id
SELECT entry_kind, COUNT(*) AS matching_entries FROM media_catalog WHERE LOWER(entry_title) LIKE LOWER('%hitch%') GROUP BY entry_kind ORDER BY entry_kind

checks.sql: SELECT entry_id, entry_title, entry_kind FROM media_catalog ORDER BY entry_id
